The Palantir stock price rally has been supported by renewed interest in its AI strategy. D.A. Davidson recently raised its price target to $250 from $200, citing growing customer interest in AI sovereignty and the company's role in helping businesses manage AI models and data.
has also added to that narrative.

Fundamentally, Palantir’s second-quarter results remain a key part of the bull case as the revenue jumped 94% YoY to $1.94B, while the U.S. commercial revenue surged 149%, and net dollar retention reached about 157%, pointing to strong expansion among existing customers.
It also raised its FY2026 U.S. commercial revenue outlook to more than $3.42B.
That growth, however, comes with a demanding valuation. Currently the stock has a D valuation grade, compared with A growth, A+ profitability, B+ momentum, and B revisions, as per
Seeking Alpha analyst Oakoff Investments believes the recovery could have further room if the stock continues beating estimates but highlights valuations as the central risk.
Technically, Palantir's price has climbed from about $174 to $192.50 on a weekly chart, with higher highs and higher lows supported by stronger volume.

Its RSI is at 48.65, and a slightly negative MACD now points to cooling momentum. The key test is the $194 resistance zone, followed by the psychological $200 level, while $188 is the key support area.
Holding the support area would keep the short-term uptrend intact, while a break below that zone could weaken the setup.
Meanwhile, Michael Burry’s renewed bearish position in the stock adds another layer to the debate around Palantir’s valuation and the durability of the AI boom.
The stock’s next move will ultimately depend on whether earnings growth continues to justify its premium multiple.
